source_resolution: Runtime captured generic unidentified-device text and weight3, while installed definition identifies matte ionic plastifer, finger-rest hilt, energy cell and weight2. Preserve both; reason for observed weight difference unknown. Charge state not exported here.

donor_reference.name: Longsword
donor_reference.role: Actual extracted Core longsword: economical long-blade silhouette, hilt and flat held-item outline convention. Qud material/finger-rest/palette override polished metal and crossguard. No donor combat logic.

rejected_reference.role: Inspected actual Vanilla Weapons Expanded knife; blade proportions too short. Core longsword selected instead.

design: Long narrow matte pointed blade, source root grooves, finger-rest hilt and short lower grip. No serrations, engraved runes, emissive aura, exaggerated crossguard or invented cell placement. Grooves interpret sparse root pixels rather than asserting unseen mechanism.
authored_scale: Approximately450 source pixels /42 pixels in48x96 view. Readable authored size, not a dimension inferred from weight.

frame.physical_scale: One common world/pixel scale calibrated to the existing female SOUTH head width, including ears, at alpha>128. Authored family-scale choice, not a recovered native height.
frame.units: width and center_x are Qud cell-width units (2/3 world); height and center_z are world units. No per-facing rescale.

palette.detail_assignment: Primary matte blade / source-native contrasting hilt. Separate equal-RGB neutral textures; no teal or glow baked in.

assembly_boundary: Only current authoring display is fitted here. Resting/ready angle/state implementation and review stay in Stage3 final assembly after all generation, per skill/user priority.
native_acceptance: Pending full-generation gate, actual named Hand292/2, west far-side, equipped and resting/ready state acceptance.

reused_generation.reason: Unchanged independent item source; only body/hand registration changes. Prior contextual body is ordinary-human reference, never claimed as a new-body generation.
